questions.question: When you are about to pass a vehicle on the left, which part of your lane should you ride in?

options.text: Right
Center
Left

questions.correctAnswerText: Left
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when you are about to pass another vehicle on the left.

questions.question: If you carry a passenger on your motorcycle, what should you do with tire pressure?

options.text: Reduce the tire pressure.
Make no tire pressure adjustments.
Increase the tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You need to increase tire pressure by a few pounds. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure.

questions.question: When you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to tell the other vehicle to go.
You should drive through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What is a main cause of single-vehicle motorcycle crashes?

options.text: Riding too fast for weather conditions.
Turning too wide in a curve or turn.
Running off the road to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning too wide in a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: A main cause of single-vehicle crashes is turning too wide in a curve or turn. This can cause a motorcycle to leave the road or hit an object.

questions.question: How should you position your body on the motorcycle?

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
Stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so your arms steer the motorcycle, not hold you up. Your elbows should be slightly bent when you hold the handgrips.

questions.question: When carrying a load on your motorcycle, where should you secure it?

options.text: As high as possible.
As low as possible.
On a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Secure loads low to keep the motorcycle balanced.

questions.question: What is true about operating a motorized scooter?

options.text: You can only use it during the day.
You can operate it without a driver license.
You can operate it with any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can operate it with any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any class of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.
Only stop to yield to other traffic.
Vehicles will be entering the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to all traffic and pedestrians, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: They see you.
It doesn't guarantee they will yield to you.
It guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It doesn't guarantee they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that eye contact means a driver will yield to you. A driver can look directly at you and still fail to see you.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the center portion of the lane:

options.text: The driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
The driver usually cannot see you.
You should avoid this position.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position increases your visibility.

questions.question: When carrying a load, where should it be secured?

options.text: As low as possible.
As high as possible.
On a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Loads should be secured as low as possible. Attaching a load to a sissy bar raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and can upset its balance.

questions.question: When the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Proceed slowly.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, you must stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you:

options.text: May go 10 mph over the speed limit.
Must stay within the speed limit.
Must ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stay within the speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must complete a pass while staying within the posted speed limit. Only pass when it is safe and legal.

questions.question: A front wheel wobble or shaking usually comes from:

options.text: Wrong tire pressure or uneven loading.
Front wheel not tightened properly.
Hitting something with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wrong tire pressure or uneven loading.
questions.explanation: A wobble is when the front wheel and handlebars shake side to side. This usually happens because of wrong tire pressure, bad loading, or unsuitable accessories.

questions.question: What separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, how does a motorcycle respond to turns?

options.text: More slowly than usual.
More quickly than usual.
Normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to the motorcycle. With extra weight, the motorcycle responds more slowly to turns, speed changes, and braking.

questions.question: Where is a motorcycle most likely to have a crash with other traffic?

options.text: On the highway.
At intersections.
On rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most crashes happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. Ride carefully and stay alert at all intersections.

questions.question: To stay safe on a long trip, you should:

options.text: Ride as far as possible in one day.
Stop as little as possible.
Avoid using artificial stimulants.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid using artificial stimulants.
questions.explanation: Avoid artificial stimulants because they cause extreme tiredness when they wear off. Limit riding to six hours per day and rest at least every two hours. Dress to protect against wind and rain.

questions.question: What formation is best for a group of riders to stay together safely?

options.text: Single file.
Riding in pairs.
Staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets a group of riders stay close together while giving each rider enough space to stay safe.

questions.question: If the front wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Keep the front wheel locked until you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the brake immediately and then apply it again.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane is ending.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop your motorcycle until the animal loses interest.
Slow down as the dog approaches, then speed up quickly as it gets close.
Swerve around the animal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as the dog approaches, then speed up quickly as it gets close.
questions.explanation: If a dog approaches your motorcycle, slow down and downshift. Then speed up quickly as the dog gets close to you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Provide a narrow view of the road behind you.
Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
Are illegal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors. They make objects look farther away than they really are. Get used to your mirrors if your motorcycle has them.

questions.question: One problem with riding next to another vehicle is:

options.text: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
Other drivers can see you easily.
You may not be able to read signs on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. The vehicle could move into your lane and hit you. It could also block your way out if something goes wrong.

questions.question: When turning, you should:

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head, not your shoulders, to look through the turn.
Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders, to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level. Turning your shoulders can make you steer the wrong way.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Need less room to stop than larger vehicles.
Need as much room to stop as larger vehicles.
Can stop instantly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need as much room to stop as larger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Always leave enough space to stop safely based on road conditions. Motorcycles need as much stopping space as other vehicles.

questions.question: Hearing protection:

options.text: Is not needed when wearing a helmet.
Is only recommended for long trips.
Should be used on every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used on every ride.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can harm your hearing even with a helmet. Wear hearing protection every time you ride.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Look over their shoulder when taking a turn or curve.
Never hold onto the rider.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over their shoulder when taking a turn or curve.
questions.explanation: Before riding, tell your passenger to look over your shoulder in the direction of any turn or curve. This helps both of you lean the right way.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders to see better.
Turn your shoulders, but not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.
